handbookNote: Nebraska Real Estate Broker license exam. Part of the 2026-09-03 R26 population-tier broker buildout (population order: UT > NV > IA > AR > KS > MS > ID > NE > WV > HI > NH > MT > RI > DE > SD > ND > AK > VT > WY). Exam vendor: Pearson VUE, under contract with the Nebraska Real Estate Commission (NREC). Exam mechanics confirmed via Pearson VUE's own official Candidate Handbook #092800 (April 2025). National/general portion: 80 scored items (+5 pretest), 2.5 hours. Nebraska state portion (Broker): 50 scored items (+5-10 pretest), 1.5 hours. Total 130 scored items, 4 hours. Passing score is a LITERAL percent-correct: 75%, on EACH section independently -- UNLIKE Kansas/Idaho, a Nebraska broker candidate who fails EITHER section must retake the ENTIRE exam (salespersons may retake just the failed portion, brokers may not). track_registry models this as exam_question_count=130, exam_duration_sec=14400, pass_percent=75, min_correct=98 (round(130*0.75)) -- unlike most peer states here, Nebraska's 75% actually IS literal, so this is a faithful model, not an approximation. NATIONAL PORTION (80 items) reuses the exact same real Pearson VUE national item bank as Utah/Nevada/Kansas/Idaho -- Nebraska's real Broker outline weights are IDENTICAL (10/8/10/15/12/9/8/8 across the same 8 sections) -- files copied directly rather than redrafted. NEBRASKA STATE PORTION (50 items, real Broker item counts): Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission (5, no Nebraska Recovery Fund exists -- confirmed absent), Licensing (7, real 2-year salesperson experience + 60 additional education-hour broker requirement), Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees (18, largest section -- real 72-hour trust-deposit rule, disciplinary grounds under Neb. Rev. Stat. 81-885.24), Agency (15) -- IMPORTANT CORRECTION found during drafting: Nebraska's agency/brokerage-relationship law is NOT in the Real Estate License Act (81-885 series) as originally assumed -- it's a wholly separate statute, Neb. Rev. Stat. 76-2401 to 76-2430 ('Agency Relationships'), including a real 2025 amendment (effective 7/1/2025) requiring a WRITTEN buyer-representation agreement for 1-4 unit residential purchases (76-2422(3)(a)), and Agency (5, landlord-tenant/URLTA, property condition disclosure 76-2,120, documentary stamp tax, Trust Deeds Act non-judicial foreclosure). Governing law: Nebraska Real Estate License Act (Neb. Rev. Stat. 81-885 to 81-885.56) for licensing/discipline, and the separate Agency Relationships article (Neb. Rev. Stat. 76-2401-2430) for agency/brokerage-relationship law. This bank was drafted across 5 new state-topic drafting passes (the 8 national files were reused, not redrafted). Answers were deterministically rotated into final A/B/C/D position via scripts/tracks/rotate_broker_answers.js.
